note: Prep for today's cases: short anaesthetic points per procedure group, matched to OT list procedure names. Articles verified on PubMed. Plain revision notes; follow department protocols.

items.title: TURP & endoscopic urology
points: Spinal to about T10 is the usual choice: an awake patient shows early TURP syndrome (restlessness, confusion, nausea, visual change) before it becomes severe.
TURP syndrome = absorption of irrigating fluid through open prostatic venous sinuses: fluid overload, dilutional hyponatraemia and, with 1.5% glycine, glycine toxicity (transient blindness).
Risk rises with long resection (over about an hour), a high irrigation bag, a large gland and capsular perforation.
Bipolar resection with saline removes the hyponatraemia risk but not the fluid overload risk.
Check serum sodium if symptoms appear; stop resection, control bleeding, and treat severe symptomatic hyponatraemia with hypertonic saline under close monitoring.
Bladder perforation in an awake patient: sudden abdominal or shoulder-tip pain, sometimes with hypotension or bradycardia.
Elderly patients: cold irrigant causes hypothermia; watch bleeding and postoperative delirium.

read.title: Hawary A et al. Transurethral resection of the prostate syndrome: almost gone but not forgotten. J Endourol 2009

items.title: Laparoscopic & robotic abdominal surgery
points: CO2 pneumoperitoneum (usually 12–15 mmHg) raises SVR and blood pressure and can lower cardiac output, more so in heart disease.
Lung compliance and FRC fall and airway pressures rise: use PEEP and raise minute ventilation as end-tidal CO2 climbs.
Insufflation can cause vagal bradycardia or asystole: ask the surgeon to deflate, give atropine.
Watch for CO2 embolism (sudden fall in end-tidal CO2 with hypotension), capnothorax and surgical emphysema.
Head-down tilt can push the tube into the right main bronchus: recheck air entry after positioning.
Robotic cases: steep tilt, docked robot and limited access to the patient; protect eyes and pressure points and plan lines before docking.
Give PONV prophylaxis and plan for shoulder-tip pain.

read.title: Atkinson TM et al. Cardiovascular and ventilatory consequences of laparoscopic surgery. Circulation 2017

items.title: Shoulder arthroscopy & surgery
points: Interscalene block gives excellent analgesia but blocks the phrenic nerve on that side in almost every patient: caution in significant lung disease.
Diaphragm-sparing options: superior trunk or suprascapular-based blocks, with less complete analgesia.
Beach-chair position risks cerebral hypoperfusion: a cuff on the arm reads higher than the pressure at the brain, roughly 0.8 mmHg for every cm the head is above the cuff.
Sitting position plus interscalene block can trigger sudden hypotension and bradycardia (Bezold–Jarisch type reflex).
Lateral decubitus position is the alternative some surgeons use; check traction and pressure points.

read.title: Hewson DW et al. Regional anaesthesia for shoulder surgery. BJA Educ 2019

items.title: Knee & hip arthroplasty
points: Spinal anaesthesia is common; add multimodal analgesia.
Knee: adductor canal block and periarticular infiltration give analgesia while keeping the quadriceps working for early mobilisation.
Tranexamic acid reduces blood loss and transfusion.
Tourniquet (knee): tourniquet pain over time; on deflation expect a fall in blood pressure and a rise in end-tidal CO2.
Cemented components carry a risk of bone cement implantation syndrome: be ready at cementing.
Elderly patients: delirium, VTE prophylaxis and early mobilisation matter.

read.title: de Carvalho CC et al. Anaesthesia and analgesia for total knee arthroplasty. BJA Educ 2026
Haslam N et al. Perioperative care of patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty. BJA Educ 2024

items.title: Hip fracture surgery
points: Frail, elderly patients: aim for surgery without delay once optimised.
Fascia iliaca or femoral nerve block helps analgesia before and after surgery.
Spinal or general anaesthesia are both acceptable; avoid hypotension.
Cemented hemiarthroplasty: risk of bone cement implantation syndrome; plan with the surgeon.

read.title: Shelton C, White S. Anaesthesia for hip fracture repair. BJA Educ 2020

items.title: Tracheostomy
points: Shared airway: agree the plan and the communication steps with the surgeon beforehand.
Airway fire risk: no diathermy to open the trachea, and lower the FiO2 before the tracheal incision if oxygenation allows.
Withdraw the tracheal tube under vision until the cuff is just above the stoma, ready to re-advance it if needed.
Confirm the tracheostomy tube with waveform capnography before removing the tracheal tube.
After surgery: a displaced new tracheostomy is an emergency; know the emergency tracheostomy algorithm.

read.title: Lewith H, Athanassoglou V. Update on management of tracheostomy. BJA Educ 2019

items.title: GI endoscopy (OGD, colonoscopy, EUS, ERCP)
points: Usually sedation with propofol and a shared airway: monitor with capnography for moderate or deep sedation.
Higher aspiration risk (achalasia, upper GI bleed, gastric outlet obstruction): consider tracheal intubation.
ERCP is often prone or semi-prone and long: think about airway access before starting.
Endoscopy suites are remote locations: same monitoring standards, check equipment and how to get help.

read.title: Sneyd JR. Developments in procedural sedation for adults. BJA Educ 2022
Henriksson AM, Thakrar SV. Anaesthesia and sedation for ERCP. BJA Educ 2022

items.title: Interventional radiology & cath lab
points: Remote location: same monitoring standards as theatre; check the machine, suction, drugs and how to call for help before starting.
Radiation safety: time, distance and shielding (lead apron, thyroid shield, mobile screens). Dose falls with the square of distance.
Contrast: ask about previous reactions, renal function and metformin.
Patients must lie flat and still, sometimes for long periods: plan sedation versus general anaesthesia early.
Carotid stenting: balloon inflation can cause bradycardia and hypotension; keep the patient awake enough for neuro checks if planned.

read.title: Lalabekyan B et al. Principles of radiation safety for anaesthetists. BJA Educ 2025

items.title: Operative hysteroscopy
points: Distension fluid is absorbed into the circulation: hypotonic media (glycine, sorbitol) cause dilutional hyponatraemia; saline causes fluid overload.
Track the fluid deficit throughout. Commonly used stop limits in healthy women: about 1000 mL for hypotonic and 2500 mL for isotonic media, lower in the elderly or those with comorbidity.
Other complications: uterine perforation, bleeding and gas embolism.
Check sodium if the deficit is large or the patient is symptomatic.

read.title: Elahmedawy H, Snook NJ. Complications of operative hysteroscopy: an anaesthetist's perspective. BJA Educ 2021

items.title: Inguinal & femoral hernia
points: Adults: general anaesthesia (often with an LMA), spinal, or local infiltration with sedation are all options.
Ilioinguinal–iliohypogastric or TAP block helps analgesia after open repair.
Laparoscopic repair carries the pneumoperitoneum issues of any laparoscopy.
Ex-premature infants: risk of postoperative apnoea, highest below about 60 weeks postmenstrual age; consider awake spinal and apnoea monitoring afterwards.

read.title: Ahmad N, Greenaway S. Anaesthesia for inguinal hernia repair in the newborn or ex-premature infant. BJA Educ 2018

items.title: Paediatric surgery
points: Weight-based everything: drugs, fluids, tube size; check your calculations twice.
Caudal or epidural blocks give good analgesia for lower abdominal and perineal surgery; mind the total local anaesthetic dose.
Spinal anaesthesia in infants is short-lasting; plan the surgery time.
Ex-premature infants: postoperative apnoea risk.

read.title: Greaney D, Everett T. Paediatric regional anaesthesia: updates in central neuraxial techniques and thoracic and abdominal blocks. BJA Educ 2019

items.title: Anal & perianal surgery
points: Saddle block (low-dose spinal in the sitting position) suits most short perianal procedures.
Under light general anaesthesia, anal stretch can trigger laryngospasm or bradycardia: keep the plane deep enough.
Lithotomy or prone jack-knife position: check pressure points and, prone, the airway.
